evals.prompt: We just wrapped our two-week sprint and it's retro time. Team of 5, all remote. Honestly it was rough — half the stories carried over again, and people are frustrated. Can you run the retro with me?
evals.expected_output: Picks iteration-retro mode and notes the remote + high-frustration context (emotion-first format like Mad/Sad/Glad or anonymous input, silent writing before discussion). Asks about / reviews previous retro actions before new topics. Gathers objective data (carry-over numbers, planned vs shipped) before feelings. Digs the carry-over symptom to a systemic cause (planning realism, WIP, unclear stories) rather than 'team was slow'. Ends with 1-3 specific owned actions with deadlines and writes a retros/YYYY-MM-DD.md artifact. No blame of individuals anywhere.
expectations: Sprint (iteration) retro mode is named before questions start
Previous retro actions are asked about or reviewed before new topics
An emotion-first or anonymous-input format is chosen because of the stated frustration
Objective data (carried-over stories, velocity, timeline) is gathered before opinions
Between 1 and 3 owned actions are written to a retro file

evals.prompt: prod was down for about 40 minutes yesterday because a db migration locked the users table during peak hours. the on-call engineer ran it manually at 2pm. we need to write this up for the team
evals.expected_output: Switches to incident-postmortem mode (reads references/variants.md). Produces a blameless postmortem doc: impact quantified, timestamped timeline, contributing factors (no single root cause hunt), trigger vs causes distinguished, detection, lessons learned incl. where-we-got-lucky, action items table with owner/priority. Does NOT blame the on-call engineer — asks how running it at 2pm made sense (no guardrail? no staging run? no runbook?). No 'should have' language in the doc.
expectations: Incident-postmortem mode is selected
The write-up has a timestamped timeline and a quantified impact (about 40 minutes, peak hours)
Contributing factors are listed and trigger is distinguished from causes
The on-call engineer is not blamed by name as the cause
Actions are owned and written to a file

evals.prompt: friday afternoon. before I log off, give me a quick retro on my week in this repo
evals.expected_output: Solo/session mode. Mines the repo itself (git log --since, branches, reverts, repeated fix attempts) instead of only asking the user. Interviews briefly with a solo-suitable format (went well / didn't / change, or 4Ls). Checks for a previous retro file and reviews its actions if present. Keeps it short (~weekly cadence scale), lands on 1-3 concrete owned actions for next week, writes the dated retro file. No self-blame framing.
expectations: Solo mode is selected and git history (git log --since, branches, reverts) is read before asking the user
The interview uses a short solo-suitable format
A previous retro file is checked for before writing a new one
1 to 3 owned actions are written to a retro file

evals.prompt: the launch is done, thank god. we should probably do some kind of lessons learned thing with everyone before people forget what happened
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a project/milestone retro (months of history, cross-functional 'everyone'). Proposes timeline reconstruction before judgments, plans safety (Prime Directive framing, anonymous input if needed, manager question), budgets more than a 60-min slot. Output is organizational lessons plus owned actions, not next-sprint tweaks. Does not run a generic start/stop/continue on a whole launch.
expectations: Project retro mode is selected
A timeline reconstruction is proposed before judgments
Psychological safety measures (Prime Directive framing, anonymous input) are planned
The session is budgeted for longer than a standard 60-minute sprint retro

evals.prompt: sprint 14 just closed for the payments squad. we planned 11 stories, shipped 6, and 3 of those carried over from sprint 13 too. can you run the retro with me and write it up? 5 people, all remote
evals.expected_output: Names iteration mode, reviews the previous retro actions, gathers objective data before feelings, digs the carry-over to a systemic cause, and writes a dated retro file with 1-3 owned actions.
expectations: The mode (iteration/sprint) is named before retro questions start
Actions from the previous retro are reviewed, or the absence of a previous retro is stated, before new topics
Objective data (planned vs shipped, carry-over) is gathered or discussed before subjective opinions are asked
At least one theme is traced to a systemic cause, and no cause names a person as the problem
A retro file is written to disk (retros/YYYY-MM-DD.md or the project's docs convention) with an actions table of 1 to 3 actions, each with an owner and a due date

evals.prompt: the checkout outage from nov 3 is fixed and we're back to normal. about 40 min of 500s after the on-call engineer pushed a config change to the api-gateway at 2pm. we need to write up what we learn, blameless please
evals.expected_output: Switches to incident postmortem mode and produces a blameless document with impact, timeline, contributing factors and 1-3 owned actions, without blaming the on-call engineer.
expectations: The mode is named as incident postmortem and references/variants.md is read or its structure (timeline, contributing factors) is used
The document contains a timeline and a contributing-factors section rather than a single root cause
No sentence blames the on-call engineer or uses 'should have' / 'failed to' wording; the document asks how the action made sense at the time
Between 1 and 3 actions are written, each with an owner and a deadline
A postmortem file is written to disk

evals.prompt: how did this coding session go, be honest. look at the last 30 commits in this repo, I feel like I reverted and redid the same fix a bunch of times
evals.expected_output: Runs a solo/session retro: mines git history for friction signals, interviews the user briefly, and writes a short retro file with 1-3 owned actions.
expectations: The mode is named as solo/session retro
Git history is read (e.g. git log, reverts) before the user is asked for opinions
Friction signals such as reverts or repeated fix attempts are cited from the actual history
Between 1 and 3 actions are written, each with an owner and a deadline
A dated retro file is written to disk and no action blames the user personally
